svg.title: How the weekly refresh of the lock files merges
svg.desc: On Mondays Renovate refreshes the lock files of every package manager. npm takes only versions released at least a week before. After Renovate, blueprint.py compiles the lock files of pip-compile again from uploads at least a week old, and keeps what main pins, such as the fix of a vulnerability. The check dependency-review asks PyPI and the registry of npm when each version that the refresh adds came out. Once every one is at least a week old and every check passes, the refresh merges on its own; a younger one holds it, and the check names it. The refresh of Composer and of any other package manager, which can't keep to that age, waits for the maintainer on a branch of its own.
